hook.text: Sodium is 1,000 times more abundant than lithium—and it's found literally everywhere, including in seawater.

buildup.text: Sodium-ion batteries swap lithium for sodium in the same basic cell architecture.

discovery.text: CATL announced the first commercial sodium-ion cells in 2021, targeting budget EVs and grid storage.

twist.text: Sodium cells store less energy than lithium, so they suit city cars and short-range vehicles best.

climax.text: If sodium-ion scales, it could break the world's dependence on lithium mining entirely.

punchline.text: The cheapest battery metal was hiding in the ocean all along.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of sodium-ion batteries?
options: Sodium is far more abundant and cheaper than lithium

details.summary: Sodium-ion batteries use abundant and cheap sodium instead of lithium, offering a low-cost alternative for short-range EVs and energy storage, though with lower energy density than lithium-ion cells.
details.whyItMatters: Sodium is thousands of times more abundant than lithium and available worldwide. Sodium-ion technology could democratize energy storage in regions with limited access to lithium supply chains.
takeaways: Sodium is vastly more abundant and cheaper than lithium
Energy density is lower, suiting city EVs and grid storage
CATL has begun mass production of sodium-ion battery cells

faq.question: Can sodium-ion batteries fully replace lithium-ion in EVs?
faq.answer: Likely not for long-range vehicles because their energy density is lower. However, for affordable city cars, electric two-wheelers, and stationary grid storage, sodium-ion is a compelling alternative.

faq.question: What advantages does sodium-ion have over lithium iron phosphate?
faq.answer: Sodium-ion cells perform better in cold weather, do not use lithium at all, and can be discharged to zero volts for safer transport. They are also expected to be cheaper at scale due to abundant raw materials.
